Estimated effect curve of a continuous regressor

Source: R/splines.R
effectcurve.Rd

For a regressor entered through a regression spline (splines::ns(), splines::bs()), a polynomial or linearly, returns the change in the linear predictor when the regressor moves from the reference value ref to each of values, with delta-method pointwise confidence limits. Centering at a reference is what makes the curve comparable across models: in fixed-effects fits the level is absorbed by the individual effects. The scale is the link scale: a difference in mean for the identity link, a log rate ratio for Poisson and negative binomial models, a log odds ratio for the logit link. Use plot() to draw it.

Usage

effectcurve(
  object,
  variable,
  values = NULL,
  ref = NULL,
  vcov = NULL,
  level = 0.95
)

Arguments

object

a "panglm" fit

variable

name of the regressor

values

values at which to evaluate the curve; default: 100 points between the 1st and 99th percentile of the regressor in the fit

ref

reference value; default: the median of the regressor

vcov

NULL (the covariance stored on the fit) or a type passed to vcov.panglm()

level

confidence level of the pointwise band

Value

a data frame of class "panglm_effectcurve" with columns value, estimate, se, lower and upper

See also

Other panglm methods: confint.panglm(), fitted.panglm(), glance.panglm(), logLik.panglm(), model.matrix.panglm(), partialeffects.panordered(), plot.panglm(), plot.panglm_effectcurve(), predict.panglm(), predict.panordered(), summary.panglm(), tidy.panglm(), vcov.panglm()

Examples

data(copd)
fit <- panglm(fev1 ~ splines::ns(crp, 3), data = copd,
              index = c("id", "visit"), model = "within", vcov = "cluster")
curve_crp <- effectcurve(fit, "crp")
head(curve_crp)
#>       value  estimate         se      lower     upper
#> 1 0.1000000 0.1765138 0.05858363 0.06169198 0.2913356
#> 2 0.1989899 0.1724357 0.05652094 0.06165674 0.2832148
#> 3 0.2979798 0.1683591 0.05447000 0.06159989 0.2751184
#> 4 0.3969697 0.1642853 0.05243396 0.06151665 0.2670540
#> 5 0.4959596 0.1602158 0.05041601 0.06140218 0.2590293
#> 6 0.5949495 0.1561518 0.04841943 0.06125152 0.2510522
plot(curve_crp)
